lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: packing and unpacking systems

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 5: Planning, Belongings, and Communication
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice packing and unpacking systems. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner has a real bag they will actually use soon, such as a backpack for an activity, an overnight bag, or a bag for a full day out.
materials: adult-or-local: a real bag for an upcoming trip or outing
adult-or-local: the real items that need to be packed
learner-local: paper or a notes app for recording the comparison

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain why the system you chose as better fits this particular trip, and describe one different kind of trip where the other system might actually work better.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items. | Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design a third, hybrid packing system that combines category grouping and order-of-use, apply it to the same bag, and explain in writing which single idea from each of the first two systems it borrows.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice packing and unpacking systems. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.elapsedWindow: Two short sessions across one day; no continuous monitoring
duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner has a real bag they will actually use soon, such as a backpack for an activity, an overnight bag, or a bag for a full day out.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact packing and unpacking systems decision or action.
Model move 2: Before packing, lay out everything that needs to go in the bag and look at it as a full set.
Model move 3: Pack the bag the first way, grouping items by category, so all clothing is together, all supplies are together, and so on.

Model check: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items. | Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system.

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for packing and unpacking systems.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner has a real bag they will actually use soon, such as a backpack for an activity, an overnight bag, or a bag for a full day out.
Coach direction: Before packing, lay out everything that needs to go in the bag and look at it as a full set.
Learner prompt: List everything you need to pack, and name one item on the list that is easy to forget.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Pack the bag the first way, grouping items by category, so all clothing is together, all supplies are together, and so on.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I grouped every item into a clear category before placing it in the bag.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I timed or roughly counted how long this first pack took.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain why the system you chose as better fits this particular trip, and describe one different kind of trip where the other system might actually work better.

Success checks: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items. | Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: packing and unpacking systems supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional packing and unpacking systems condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items. | Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner has a real bag they will actually use soon, such as a backpack for an activity, an overnight bag, or a bag for a full day out.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: List everything you need to pack, and name one item on the list that is easy to forget.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: packing and unpacking systems — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the packing and unpacking systems task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain why the system you chose as better fits this particular trip, and describe one different kind of trip where the other system might actually work better.
observableCriteria: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items.
Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System execution: Both the category system and the order-of-use system are applied correctly and distinctly to the same set of real items. | Comparison and reasoning: The comparison names a specific item and a real difference in how quickly or easily it was found under each system.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
